> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df7a137923be503bf6fea15a6fc944d3ba06df6f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6f3877adac2979bd0c06b471d2b781d49fb64027` — the merge of head `85abb2ed96cc910f5b29d5757f32fa933bd1ceb6` into base `df7a137923be503bf6fea15a6fc944d3ba06df6f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6f3877adac2979bd0c06b471d2b781d49fb64027 && git checkout 6f3877adac2979bd0c06b471d2b781d49fb64027
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin df7a137923be503bf6fea15a6fc944d3ba06df6f 85abb2ed96cc910f5b29d5757f32fa933bd1ceb6 && git checkout -B drift-repro df7a137923be503bf6fea15a6fc944d3ba06df6f && git merge --no-ff 85abb2ed96cc910f5b29d5757f32fa933bd1ceb6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json df7a137923be503bf6fea15a6fc944d3ba06df6f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs df7a137923be503bf6fea15a6fc944d3ba06df6f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `85abb2ed96cc910f5b29d5757f32fa933bd1ceb6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read, and nothing else: card #22957 (body; triage 6119365636; claim 6124337059; report 6125920806; seat review 6126018973), PR #23055 (body, the 3-file list, the net diff against `main` from merge base `df7a137923`), and the 40 check-runs on this head. Every required context reads `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`); `Check Changeset` and `Check PR Size` read `success`; no governed path. The spec texts cited were read on `origin/main` `ec7f7f83b6` (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, `field-value.zod.ts`, `object.zod.ts`); `engine.ts`'s readers were enumerated on `origin/main` and on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`tree` joins the delete family — right.** The spec declares it: `FieldSchema`'s `.overwrite` materializes `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` on `tree` beside `lookup` because the type "is in the relational family, where the key states delete semantics"; `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` lists `tree`; the key's own description is "What happens if referenced record is deleted". Triage ruled repair (A) and refused (B). The engine was the layer falling short; the diff fixes the engine and leaves `packages/spec` untouched, as the claim's surface requires.
2. **A `tree` resolves through the `lookup` branch (an authored value as written; absent is `set_null`) — right.** The `master_detail` branch's coercion rests on "a detail cannot outlive its master", which a hierarchy does not assert, and the spec materializes the same default on `tree` as on `lookup`. Against the declared semantics, each change:
   - an authored `restrict` on a `tree` now refuses the parent's delete with `DELETE_RESTRICTED`/409 and `dependentObject` the tree's own object — right: that refusal IS what the author wrote, and a leaf still deletes (pinned);
   - a required `tree`'s `set_null` escalates to `restrict` — right by the walk's unchanged rule (a cleared scalar foreign key trips the child's own `required` validator with a misleading 400; the escalation is a property of the resolved behaviour plus `required`, not of the type), the reading a required `lookup` has carried since #9625 (pinned);
   - `cascade` deletes the subtree — right: a tree's `reference` must name the declaring object (`refuseForeignTreeReference`), so `cascade` has no other meaning. Termination on a corrupt cycle rests on membership, not depth: `collectCascadeDeleteSet` enqueues a record only when `cascadeSetAdd` first admits it, and `walkReferencingRelations` records `entered` before the first nested delete — read on main and unchanged by the diff; pinned for 15 levels, a cycle and a self-parent.
3. **`planCascadeAtomicity` reads the same predicate — right and necessary.** A subtree cascade is several deletes, and the atomicity rule ("atomic honoured for real, or refused") would be contradicted by the one relation the walk now follows; the dev's ablation leg B shows the pin bites on its own. Consequence named, because the changeset states it and an operator will see it: an object with a `tree` field references itself, so its by-id delete never plans `'none'` again — on the default datasource every such delete opens a transaction (children or not); on another datasource `warnCascadeNotAtomic` fires once per object; on a driver without `beginTransaction` the `transaction()` degrade warns once per driver. Correct, and the CONTROL (an object nothing references opens no transaction) is pinned.
4. **Family predicate coverage — complete for the delete walk.** On `origin/main`, `engine.ts` carried the `master_detail`/`lookup` family literal at three sites: `buildSummaryIndex` (11709), `planCascadeAtomicity` (17244) and `cascadeRelationBehavior` (17838). The diff replaces the latter two with `statesDeleteSemantics`; `collectCascadeDeleteSet` and `walkReferencingRelations` read through `cascadeRelationBehavior` and need no edit. The two single-type reads left inside the walk are right as literals: the resolution ternary (`master_detail` to `cascade` unless `restrict`; everything else to the authored value or `set_null`), under which a `tree` takes the second arm by design, and the `master_detail` plus authored `set_null` error log, which is about that type alone. `buildSummaryIndex`'s literal resolves a roll-up's foreign key and is not the delete walk — right to leave. Outside `engine.ts`: no `master_detail`/`lookup` pair in `packages/objectql/src`; the dangling-reference audit reads `referenceTargetOf`, which admits `tree`; `packages/verify/src/derive.ts`'s `RELATIONAL` set already carries `tree` (which is why the instrument reported `f_tree`); `packages/rest` has no delete-walk reader. Every reader of the walk asks the one predicate.
5. **A referenceless `tree` — does nothing, and this PR is right not to decide it.** `cascadeRelationBehavior` reads the carrier through `referenceCarrierOf`, which answers `undefined` for an absent `reference`; `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS` names `user` only. The spec contradicts itself on the shape: `refuseForeignTreeReference` prescribes "Drop `reference` (it is optional on a `tree`)", while `referenceTargetOf`'s docblock calls a `tree` with no `reference` "an authoring bug". An engine that filled in the owning object would be settling that reading in a consumer (Prime Directive #12). Escalated: the seat files it at ACCEPT as class (b), measured by the dev at the REST door on this head. Reach today: `examples/app-showcase`'s `f_tree` carries `reference`, and no `tree` field exists in `packages/platform-objects` (the `org_chart` hits are views), so no shipped corpus row sits in the gap.
6. **`multiple: true`** — refused at parse on a `tree`; a raw registration is read single-valued through `isMultiValueField`, the walk's one arbiter. Right: nothing was added for a shape the contract refuses.
7. **`user` stays out** — right; the spec's `.overwrite` puts it on the non-reference side on purpose, and moving it is a declaration change.

### ② Semver level

The card's thread asks two things; both are answered from the repo's rules, not from lane memory.

- **Level: `patch` is right.** The rules this repo states for a changeset level are AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3 ("A bug fix in a released package takes a **`patch`** changeset"; the arm rule "`yes` takes at least `minor`, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING") and `pr-automation.yml`'s "WHICH LEVEL" (maintainer ruling 2026-09-04, decision batch #35, on #15294): `minor` is owed for "a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface (a new exported symbol on an `index`, a new accepted key or value)", and "a `fix(` that changes no public surface stays `patch`". `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s header adds the launch-window clause: a BREAKING change ships as `minor`, carried by the `**BREAKING**` banner plus an ADR-0087 disposition. No rule in AGENTS.md or in either changeset gate grades a behavioural change at a runtime door `minor` on its own; `minor` follows only from a widening or from a breaking declaration. This diff adds no export (`index.ts` untouched; the file list has three files) and no accepted key or value (`FieldSchema` untouched), so the widening arm is out. Whether it is BREAKING is the second question.
- **`no (narrowing)` would be wrong.** `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines the arm: the value answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, and `(narrowing)` marks "a diff that NARROWS a published accept set" — its ruling case (#16296) narrowed a payload's value domain so that something an author could write became refused. `check-adr-0087-registration` reads that arm as a breaking declaration and demands a migration disposition. This PR refuses nothing an author writes: every field that parsed on `main` parses byte-identically on this head, and the delete that now answers 409 does so because the author declared `restrict` (or declared `required` on a key whose default is `set_null`). The engine starting to perform a declared outcome is enforcement of the existing contract — triage's own words, "the runtime starts honouring a declared key, and the accept set does not change" — not a narrowing of the accept set, and there is no migration to prescribe, because the author's declaration is already the canonical shape. So `Clause-②: no` with no arm, and `patch`, are the repo-correct reading. On the precedents the seat cites (#22856, #22519, #22892, #22908 — outside this brief's inputs): if they refused authored shapes they were narrowings in the arm's sense and this PR is not one; if they did not, they graded above the rule, and AGENTS.md says a rule lives there or in the gate, nowhere else. The consumer-facing carrier the launch window relies on is present regardless: the changeset body names each behaviour an operator will see (`set_null`, `cascade`, `restrict`, the required escalation, the transaction).
- `Check Changeset` reads `success` on this head; the changeset body carries `Clause-②: no` on its own line.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation: the pins use the in-file snapshot-rollback driver of the five sibling `engine-cascade-delete-*` suites, not the real driver the claim named — **accepted**, as the seat accepted it: `packages/objectql` declares no driver dependency, and adding one is a lockfile and ledger change outside the surface. The re-runnable real-driver evidence is `os verify --delete-behaviors` on the showcase (`hardFailures` 1 to 0, `f_tree` proven at both doors, the other 23 rows identical); the `SqlDriver` scratch probe is uncommitted and therefore not evidence anyone can re-run — if the seat wants a committed real-driver pin, the dev's suggestion (`examples/app-showcase/test`) is a separate small change, not a condition here.
- Deviation: one docs-only merge of `main` (this head); the model-free trailer pair — fine under AGENTS.md.
- `open_questions`: none in 6125920806.
- Finding 1 (referenceless `tree`) — **escalated**, correctly (judgment ①5); filed by the seat at ACCEPT.
- Finding 2 (the two `field.zod.ts` comments that say the engine reads the key only behind a `master_detail`/`lookup` guard — the `deleteBehavior` TSDoc's #9784 paragraph and the `.overwrite` block's "`cascadeDeleteRelations` reaches the key exclusively on `master_detail`/`lookup` fields") — **may stay an Acceptance note on this PR, and must gain a carrier.** Reasons it stays out: the claim's surface is `engine.ts` plus tests plus one changeset ("stop on a breach"); `packages/spec` is cross-lane; a TSDoc edit on a schema is a `check:docs` trigger under AGENTS.md's "Touched `packages/spec`?" protocol, so a comment rider is the scope expansion Prime Directive #10 refuses; and the comments have no runtime consequence. Reason it needs a carrier: once this lands the sentences are false, and the `.overwrite` block's `user` sentence ("sits outside today's cascade guard exactly like `text` does") is the rationale a future reader will trust. Decision: the seat lists both sites in the spec card it files at ACCEPT for finding 1 — same file, same `tree` delete-semantics reading, one `domain:spec` card — so the note's `承接者:无` becomes a card.
- Finding 3 (an authored `deleteBehavior` on a `user` field parses and is not walked) — Acceptance note, right (the spec's own line).
- Triage's measure-at-claim list (authored `cascade`, `restrict`, `multiple: true`) — all three reported before and after; the pin triage named (`os verify --delete-behaviors` from 1 to 0 with `lookup`/`master_detail` CONTROLS unchanged) is reported row by row.
- 495 changed lines; no governed surface; nothing under `content/docs/releases/`. The docs-drift advisory lists seven hand-written pages by a `set_null` literal in a changed comment — advisory, and outside this brief's inputs; not re-verified here.

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-12T15:28Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript. It made 64 tool calls: reads, `git fetch` into review refs, and the two record writes. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. One self-check script went to the scratchpad root rather than this PR's scratch directory, and was deleted. One reviewer rendered this record and PR #23045's, each from its own brief.

Reviewed-by: `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX`

**VERDICT: PASS**
